name: Wall reset blocks
summary: Alone at a wall, drive the ball at medium pace, then absorb the faster rebound with a soft block that drops low, and count resets that stay low.
setup: Tape a line on the wall about 0.9 m above the floor (the net) and a second line about 1.3 m (the top of a low reset)
Stand about 4 m from the wall; hit a medium-pace drive above the top line
Absorb the rebound with a soft, short block (paddle face open, little backswing) so it hits the wall between the two lines
A reset counts when it lands between the lines; a block above the top line, below the net line or a miss is an error. Sets of 10
success_criterion: In each of 3 sets of 10 drive-then-block patterns, at least 7 resets land between the two lines
safety_notes: Wear eye protection. Start at medium pace and add pace only when 7 of 10 land; the rebound comes back fast at this distance, so keep the paddle up and in front. Stop if in pain.
coach_rationale: (judgment) Errors under pressure come from fast balls a player cannot take pace off (the AN-07 forced-error share); a soft block that drops low turns a hard ball into a neutral one. The wall supplies the pace a partner would otherwise feed. Unverified coaching content until a human coach reviews the library (P15).
